Exclude or reinstate individual colonies after image review

Source: R/colony-exclusions.R
exclude_colonies.Rd

Save a review decision by exact plate and colony ID. The next finish_experiment() applies it automatically. Original image measurements, detection flags and plate-level qc_pass values are not changed.

Usage

exclude_colonies(project, plate_id, colony_id, reason, exclude = TRUE)

Arguments

project

A saved FunMel project or its current folder.

plate_id, colony_id

Character vectors identifying the rejected targets. A single plate ID may be used with several colony IDs.

reason

Nonempty review reason, one per decision or one shared reason.

exclude

TRUE excludes the colony; FALSE reinstates it. One logical value or one per decision.

Value

Invisibly, the saved decision table. Decisions are written to colony_exclusions.csv beside project.rds. Repeating an ID pair updates its decision. Raw measurements are retained. Exclusions belong to the current saved image-analysis run; re-review and record them again after reanalysis.

Details

Use guided recovery first when a boundary can be corrected. A finite MI from a bad mask cannot be identified automatically. Exclusions apply to target-colony comparisons, including spot-based coefficients. With na_action="omit", remaining valid targets are used. A plate without usable targets still requires review. Review flags do not filter data. Measurements from excluded masks remain in output tables for audit and must not be interpreted as valid size, colour or spot values.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
exclude_colonies(project, plate_id="plate_1", colony_id="TR",
                 reason="Mask includes agar")
reviewed <- finish_experiment(project)
# Reinstate after reviewing the decision:
exclude_colonies(project, "plate_1", "TR",
                 reason="Rechecked; boundary is acceptable", exclude=FALSE)
} # }
